Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Travel & transport

go verb

to a place

also go to, be going, let’s go, head for

classical

Plaut. Asin. 921b: ī domum
Cic. Att. 2.14.2: Rōmam īre
Ov. Tr. 1.1.1: ībis in urbem
Traupman 322

eō, īre, iī (īvī), itum

verb, irregular

The everyday verb for going anywhere. Where to is the accusative alone for towns and small islands and for domum and rūs (Rōmam īre, domum īre, rūs īre); otherwise ad or in with the accusative (ad avum, in hortum). An errand takes the supine: cubitum, dormītum, lūsum īre (Hor. S. 1.5.48; 1.6.119). “Let’s go!” is Eāmus!

Other words

  • vādō, vādere — go, make one’s way (with purpose or haste)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.10.2: ad eum postrīdiē māne vādēbam; Vulg. Lc. 10.37: Vāde, et tū fac similiter

    (vōx in ōrātiōne solūtā rāra (Cic. Att., Liv.); apud poētās (Verg.) et in Vulgātā frequēns)

    Lewis & Short: “rare but classical”. No classical perfect.

Examples

  • Surge, amātor, ī domum.

    Up you get, lover boy, and go home.Plaut. Asin. 921b

  • C. Arrius proximus est vīcīnus, immō ille quidem jam contubernālis, quī etiam sē idcircō Rōmam īre negat ut hīc mēcum tōtōs diēs philosophētur.

    Gaius Arrius is my nearest neighbour, or rather my housemate by now: he even says he isn’t going to Rome, so that he can spend whole days here philosophising with me.Cic. Att. 2.14.2

  • dormīre quotiēns libuit, īmus ad vīllam

    whenever I want to sleep, I go off to my house in the countryMart. 12.57.28

  • Ego rūs ībō, atque ibi manēbō.

    I’ll go to the country and stay there.Ter. Eun. 216b

  • Eāmus.

    Let’s go.Traupman 339

See also go, where are we going?, where are you off to?, go to bed, go to school, go shopping, go up, go down, set out, return, continue, safe journey.
